Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

DataComp-LM: In search of the next generation of training sets for language models (2406.11794v1) · paper method: The human-quality study samples 499 rule-filtered/deduplicated documents and obtains three labels per document from 16 English-speaking AI graduate students/professors; 281 documents have unanimous labels.

cohort3.claim.dclm.human-rubric-scope

  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific author-reported study; experiments, raw dataset records and formal proofs were not independently reproduced or verified.
  • AppendixM.1 supplies the training-utility rubric, and footnote6 says annotation was voluntary and unpaid. This sample does not establish that all human annotation is ineffective.

DataComp-LM: In search of the next generation of training sets for language models (2406.11794v1) · paper method: DCLM’s first evaluation suite omits fairness, multilinguality and safety; compute limits prevent joint exploration of all curation dimensions, sufficient random-seed variation and testing beyond 7B models.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

DataComp-LM: In search of the next generation of training sets for language models (2406.11794v1) · paper method: The DCLM-Baseline quality filter uses fastText trained with OpenHermes 2.5 plus high-scoring ELI5 positives and RefinedWeb-sampled negatives, retaining the top 10% by classifier score.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

DataComp-LM: In search of the next generation of training sets for language models (2406.11794v1) · paper method: DCLM provides an unfiltered Common-Crawl-derived pool of 240T GPT-NeoX tokens and five fixed-recipe compute scales; evaluation separates 53-task extended performance, 22-task core performance and five-shot MMLU.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

DataComp-LM: In search of the next generation of training sets for language models (2406.11794v1) · paper method: For the reported 2.6T-token 7B model, the authors augment DCLM-Baseline with StarCoder and ProofPile2, use a math-enriched annealing phase and extend context; Table 9 reports 63.7% MMLU.
